title: Lesson 7: Structured Output: JSON Mode, Function Calling, and Tool Schemas Done Right
description: An agent is only as reliable as its data contracts. This lesson builds the structured-output ladder (JSON mode, Structured Outputs, function calling) and the tool-schema practices that keep tool calls valid, parseable, and safe in production.

questions.question: What does JSON mode guarantee about a response?
options: That it is valid JSON, not that it matches a schema
That every required field is present and correctly typed
That the model selected the correct tool for the task
That the response contains no markdown formatting
questions.explanation: JSON mode only ensures the output parses, so it can still have wrong keys or missing fields; you must validate against your schema to trust it.

questions.question: In tool calling, which party actually executes the tool?
options: The model, as part of generating the call
Your application code after it validates them
The provider's platform acting on the model's behalf as it generates
The tool schema itself during parsing
questions.explanation: The model only proposes a structured call; your code validates and executes it, which keeps the model safely unable to act on your systems directly.

questions.question: When is function calling the right choice over Structured Outputs?
options: When formatting the final answer that is shown to the user
When the output only needs to be valid JSON
When the model must pick and call one of your tools
When no external data is involved
questions.explanation: Function calling adds tool selection on top of schema enforcement, so use it when the output is an action to execute rather than an answer to display.
